faq.a: The Nifty 100 index represents the top 100 companies by market capitalisation listed on the National Stock Exchange (NSE). It is a broad market index reflecting the performance of large and liquid Indian companies.

faq.q: Should I stop my SIPs if the market falls?
faq.a: Generally, no. Stopping SIPs during a market fall means you miss the opportunity to buy more units at lower prices, which is crucial for rupee cost averaging and long-term wealth creation.

faq.q: When does it make sense to increase my SIP amount?
faq.a: It makes sense to increase your SIP amount if your income has risen and you have a stable financial situation. Increasing SIPs during market corrections can be particularly beneficial as it allows you to accumulate more units when prices are low.

faq.q: Is rebalancing my portfolio necessary during volatility?
faq.a: Yes, rebalancing is important to maintain your desired asset allocation. Market volatility can cause your portfolio's equity or debt component to drift significantly from your target, and rebalancing helps bring it back in line with your risk profile.

faq.q: How does rupee cost averaging benefit my investments?
faq.a: Rupee cost averaging works by ensuring you buy fewer units when prices are high and more units when prices are low, over time. This strategy helps reduce your average purchase cost per unit, potentially leading to better returns when the market recovers.

faq.q: Should I switch all my equity funds to debt funds if the market becomes volatile?
faq.a: Making drastic shifts like moving all equity to debt funds based on short-term market predictions is generally not advisable for long-term investors. Such moves can lead to missing out on market recoveries. Any changes should align with your long-term goals and risk profile.

faq.q: What role do my financial goals play in my SIP strategy?
faq.a: Your financial goals dictate your investment horizon and risk tolerance. For long-term goals, continuing equity SIPs through volatility is often appropriate. For short-term goals, you might consider de-risking your portfolio as you approach the goal.
